problem_type: A spend decision with no owner, made by whichever module happened to hold the endpoint
symptom: Clicking 保存验证 on the provider connect page immediately spends the user's credits: the credential probe sends a real POST /chat/completions with max_tokens:1, and no quote card ever appears.
direct_cause: probeDirectKeyCredential unconditionally issued whatever request the vendor seed's livenessProbe declared, and that field was serving two different questions at once: the weekly radar's per-model liveness check (which is a real generation by definition) and 'is this key valid'. APIMart's declaration was therefore a real chat completion. The request leaves through appFetch, never touching runtime.ts and carrying no grantId, so the spend gate cannot see it.
class_root: Whether an outbound call spends the user's money was never a declared property of that call. It lived in a comment beside one seed, and the endpoint itself was shared by two questions with different prices, so the cheaper question silently inherited the expensive one's cost.
affected_population: Every user connecting APIMart through the built-in provider card (the only seed whose probe was a real generation), on first save and again before first use
Every future built-in seed whose author declares a liveness probe without stating what it costs
entry_points: Save-and-verify on the built-in provider connect page (upsertVendorApiKey → validateCandidateCredential)
Pre-first-use revalidation of a pending credential (revalidatePendingCredential)
The connect page's own cost sentence, which must state the same verdict the sender uses
invariants: A credential probe that costs money is never sent without an explicit human confirmation on the existing spend card
Whether a probe is free is a declared property of the seed with a source that proves it, never an assumption; absent means paid
One module decides how a credential is verified and what that verification costs; every probe path asks it rather than judging again
The connect page's cost sentence is a projection of that same verdict, and says 'unknown' rather than 'free' when it cannot read it
Declining the paid probe stores the key as unverified instead of failing the connection
The weekly radar's per-model liveness probe and the credential-validity probe are separate declarations, so neither inherits the other's price

door_reduction.why_not: The count grows because the concept now has a named owner that every path must call, and calling it is itself a door. The decision, however, went from scattered to single: credentialProbePolicy.credentialProbePlan is the only place that answers 'how is this key verified and does verifying it cost money', and the four writes against it (directKeyCredential, validateCandidateCredential x2, onboardingIpc) are consumers, not second judgements — credentialValidationStrategy, which used to answer the same question a second time, is gone and its remaining is-this-a-builtin half is now hasBuiltinCredentialJudgement. Three doors stay outside on purpose. vendorHealth and probeAdapterCredential both probe credentials but only ever call GET /models, so they are already free; routing them through the owner today would add indirection without changing a byte, while the owner's invariant test is what keeps 'free' true for them. probeOneProtocol (electron/ai/onboarding/onboardingIpc.ts:189) genuinely does send a billable POST and is the one real gap left; it is recorded under same_class_entry_points as deferred with its reason. authorizeSpend is the canvas-side spend gate and is a different concept (grant minting for generation), kept in the map only to prove the two do not overlap.

generality_proof: Every path that can send a seed-declared credential probe now goes through probeDirectKeyCredential, which asks credentialProbePlan before it builds a request; a repository-wide search finds no other consumer of VendorSeed.livenessProbe. The seed invariants test additionally scans every built-in seed and fails when a direct-key seed omits cost or declares a generation-shaped endpoint as free, so the class is closed at declaration time rather than at call time.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the single answer to 'how is this vendor's key verified, and does verifying it spend the user's money'
Ask the one existing spend card, priced by the one existing quote owner, and fail closed when nobody can be asked

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Returns early for a paid plan: a billable probe is only ever started by the user's explicit save-and-verify click, never by a moment we picked ourselves.
Its only outbound call is fetchModelList (GET /models), which costs nothing; the file's own header states zero quota as the reason it can afford to probe every vendor on every panel open.

The certification flow's credential step is also fetchModelList only; the billable part of that flow is the separate Model self-check, which is a deliberate user-started certification run, not a credential probe.

It sends a real POST /chat/completions (or /responses, or /v1/messages) to detect which wire protocol a user-supplied relay speaks, and a model list cannot answer that question, so it cannot simply be made free. Routing it through the owner means putting a confirmation card in front of every custom-relay 测试连接 in a release-blocking lane, and the card fails closed when the renderer bridge is unreachable, which would turn the custom-vendor wizard into a dead end. Recorded as its own TODO line rather than changed here.

Another session owns this file this week (fix/vendor-connection-identity-20260922); touched read-only per the agreed avoidance. Its credential step is already free; its model step is a real generation that belongs to the certification concept, not the credential-probe one.

recurrence.reason: Any outbound call whose cost is documented in prose rather than declared in the call itself will eventually be sent by a layer that cannot read the prose. T-MO-20 already paid $0.439 for the same shape when a generation endpoint was used as a balance probe.
same_class_scan: door-map probeDirectKeyCredential validateCandidateCredential vendorHealth authorizeSpend credentialProbePlan confirmCredentialProbeSpend probeOneProtocol probeAdapterCredential --roots=electron,src
Read every outbound call reachable from a credential-validation entry point and classified each as free (GET /models, balance, estimate) or billable (chat/completions, generations)

prevention.invariant: Cost is part of the probe declaration; absent means paid, and paid means a human is asked before a byte goes out.
prevention.failure_mode: A new seed that forgets to declare cost is treated as paid, so the worst case is an unnecessary confirmation card, never a silent charge. The seed invariants test turns that omission red for built-in vendors at declaration time.
prevention.strategy: Move the money question out of a comment and into the declaration, then give it one reader that every sender must consult.

legacy_paths.rationale: credentialValidationStrategy, the second dispatcher that also answered 'how is this key verified', no longer exists; the one question it still needed to answer for the publish path is now the is-this-a-builtin predicate hasBuiltinCredentialJudgement. APIMart's generation-shaped liveness probe is replaced outright, not kept behind a flag, so there is no declaration left from which the paid call could be re-derived.

migration: No persisted data changes. A credential already stored as verificationPending under the old paid probe is simply re-checked against the free endpoint the next time it is used.
residual_risks: The paid branch has no built-in vendor in it today (both seeds that declare a probe are free), so its production coverage rests on the fail-closed default plus the loopback fixture in the regression test. That is deliberate: the branch exists because the default is fail-closed, not because a shipping vendor needs it.

GET /v1/balance proves the key is accepted and shows the remaining balance; it does not prove the account can afford a particular generation. That is the same limit Higgsfield's estimate probe carries and is stated beside both declarations.

invariant_owner_layer.rationale: It is the only layer holding both the seed declaration and the vendor identity, so it is the only layer that can answer the cost question before a request is built.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency is involved; the fix is entirely inside this repository's own modules.

external_sources.purpose: Establish that APIMart exposes a free, key-scoped validity endpoint (GET /v1/balance) and what its success body looks like, so the credential probe no longer has to send a real generation.
Confirm the account endpoints exist in the official API manual before trusting a single reference page.
Back the free declaration on Higgsfield's /estimate probe: it returns a price and never queues a job.
